# Stage 2 independent acceleration branch — 2026-11-18

Server checkout: `/data1/users/liugang/src/eq-bpe/project/runs/stage2_acceleration_20261118/code`.
Local files here are an overlay for that checkout, not a standalone Python package.
Existing stage2_main_v1 local files and running server training snapshots were not edited.

Implemented in the independent checkout:

- FastBackend in the existing bounded SafeBackend worker; independently enabled only in this branch.
- Bounded compilation LRU (512 terms), parsed-system LRU (128 systems), term-value LRU (128 MiB), and fit-result LRU (256 entries).
- Fit caches fingerprint visible arrays, halo, coordinates, time and masks. No future fields used; modified visible inputs invalidate derivative and result caches.
- Conservative equation/field dependency matching rejects systems that cannot match three independent equations to three fields. Passing does not prove numerical rank or well-posedness. It permits algebraic constraints and does not impose NS.
- Exact-text score cache scoped to one candidate-selection call; original accepted-candidate count and repeated-candidate semantics preserved. Equivalent but nonidentical texts are not merged.
- Candidate progress writes throttled to 20 attempts plus completion. Individual worker progress remains unchanged.
- Batched autoregressive generation is opt-in. Completed rows are removed from later forward passes; legal-token transitions are cached per sampling call. Batch 1 remains the default.
- Bounded, role-scoped LRU caching of immutable visible windows for both NPZ and prepared NPY readers. Targets remain uncached and test access barriers are unchanged.

Unchanged: reward formula, coefficient anchors, 32-window full scoring, candidate budget 400, SFT schedule, splits, stopping/test barriers, numerical discretization and rollout. Structural filtering is an intentional change in candidate admission, independently switchable with structural_gate=False in FastBackend for equivalence benchmarks. No coarse-window rejection, duplicate-free success budget, asynchronous worker pool or GPU scoring has been implemented.

Verification: 67 server tests passed, including coefficient/R2/forecast equivalence, cache invalidation with reused window labels, missing field-matching rejection, visible-window cache role scoping, exact-text score-cache semantics, and compacted batch-sampler generation.

Small CPU benchmarks (one train_fit window, one thread, nice 15):

- Three simple systems: original repeat fit pass ~0.0303 s; cached ~0.0083 s; first cached pass slightly slower. This is a repeat workload, not whole-run speedup.
- Five real batch-1 Top10 formulas: original cold parse+fit 0.662 s and repeated pass 0.391 s; accelerated 0.443 s and 0.0139 s. Coefficients and R2 matched at rtol/atol 1e-10. Structural gate disabled during this comparison to hold candidate set constant.

Limits: CPU benchmarks are small same-window replays, not whole-run speedups. GPU0 is shared with another user's process and the 5% cap was used. Batched stochastic draws differ from serial seeds, so batch size changes the proposal stream even though constraints and scoring stay fixed. GPU timing depends on token lengths and shared-device scheduling.

## GPU0 follow-up (explicit user authorization to share GPU0)

Implemented opt-in `sample_many`/`sampling_batch_size` (default 1), per-call legal-token-state cache, and removal of completed rows from autoregressive forward batches. Generated/evaluated/unused candidate counts are reported separately. Batched random streams differ from serial per-candidate seeds, so batch size remains explicit and does not change existing run configs. Checkpoint token budget is 1024; an early benchmark JSON incorrectly labeled it 256 (load restored 1024); optimized output reports actual 1024.

GPU0 benchmark: fixed frozen 811/v128 checkpoint, model-only sampling, five measured repetitions per batch size after warmup, 5% allocator memory cap, nice 15 and one CPU thread. Shared GPU measurements have scheduling variance.

|Batch|Original aggregate seconds|Optimized seconds|Speedup|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|1|2.448|2.095|1.17x|
|4|37.537|21.470|1.75x|
|8|179.030|52.389|3.42x|

Generated lengths and valid counts matched for all benchmark streams. Separate GPU record-by-record comparisons for batch1 seed20261300 and batch4 seed20261600 matched exactly (raw text, reason, generated count and state metadata). This is evidence on these streams, not bitwise reproducibility across all hardware/batch shapes. Allocated peak fell 2401.6 -> 669.0 MiB; reserved peak 4866 -> 1904 MiB. Added CPU tests bring total to 66 passing tests.

A 256MiB visible-window LRU was added to both NPZ and prepared NPY readers with immutable arrays and role-scoped authorization checks.

## Cancelled Main Run

On 2026-11-18 the user explicitly cancelled the Stage 2 run. Its four workers and supervisor were stopped; completed batch JSONs, logs, progress, resume files, and checkpoints remain under `runs/stage2_main_full_v2_safe_20261116`. A stop snapshot is at `runs/stage2_main_full_v2_safe_20261116_cancelled_snapshot_20261118`. Queue status is marked `cancelled=true` and retains the two jobs that had been pending.

Six isolated configs and a matrix are staged in this branch's `configs/` and `matrix.json`: same candidate budget, reward, full-window scoring, SFT schedule and splits; opt-in sampling batch 4, visible cache 256 MiB, structural field-matching gate, GPU0, two workers, 5% CUDA memory fraction per worker. They were not launched. Resume from old checkpoints requires an explicit review because the structural gate and sampling stream change candidate admission and order.

## Approved staged-search policy — 2026-11-18

User approved 4-window coarse fits, top 50% fine evaluation, 400 fine-qualified candidates; then approved concrete 64->32 pools and dual term/tree penalty.

Implemented `search_policy.py` and runner integration:

- Per current training batch, choose four visible training windows by seeded selection, distinct trajectories where possible. No selection based on field values; no future targets or test access.
- Fill a pool of 64 parsed, structurally admissible and finite coarse-fit candidates. Coarse fits do not introduce a per-equation R2 gate. Rank by the new complexity-weighted mean R2 and keep the top 32 (stable tie order).
- Fine evaluation uses all windows in the current training batch (normally 32; last batch uses its actual size), retaining the original fine fit gate. Continue pools until 400 fine-qualified candidates, within the original generation-attempt cap. Incomplete budget is recorded as failure, never padded with fallback formulas.
- Final Top10 and SFT use fine reward only. The original mean-R2 aggregation remains; no weakest-equation objective or new rollout filter is added. Existing epoch-end validation remains, with the same dual complexity factor replacing its old term-only factor.
- Reward: mean_R2 * max(0,1 - 0.3 log10(T)) * exp(-0.005*N). T is original canonical term count. N counts tuple AST nodes of normalized residual-support trees before finite-difference expansion, including add/operation/variable/constant nodes; scalar metadata such as derivative-axis strings are not separate nodes. Tree depth is logged only. No NS templates, required time-derivative roles, viscosity signs or physical terms are imposed.
- Candidate-by-candidate coarse/fine decisions are appended to screening/*.jsonl. Timing separates generation+coarse fit and fine fit. Exact-text caches are scoped to current scoring context.
- Six staged configs updated; no new formal training launched. Old experiment remains cancelled with artifacts retained.

Verification: 70 server unit/regression tests passed after policy integration. Policy tests check deterministic 4-window selection, 64->32 ordering, full fine-window scoring, complexity monotonicity and absence of future access. Real-data CPU smoke passed through bounded SafeBackend and four train_fit prefixes, including transfer of tree metrics. Smoke result is infrastructure validation, not a quality claim.

Cost caveat: for one pool, raw fit calls decrease from 64*32=2048 to 64*4+32*32=1280 (37.5%). For 400 fine-qualified candidates, more coarse candidates are generated; end-to-end speedup is not established. Coarse/fine overlap may reuse fit caches. Profiling and screening recall audits are still needed. Solver/boundary method changes beyond existing diagnostics have not been made in this policy update.

## Whole-path follow-up audit (2026-11-18)

Added inference-only `incremental.py`: KV storage per unchanged decoder layer, one-token embedding/attention/FFN/projection per generation step, with cache row selection when candidates finish. Training forward and saved model tensors remain unchanged. `generator.use_kv_cache=true` is now staged in all six configs; inference only, never used by SFT. Full-prefix inference remains available via false. A 2048-entry tokenization LRU avoids re-tokenizing unchanged SFT formulas; callers receive fresh lists to preserve mutation semantics. Sampling skips repeated prefix decoding when EOS cannot structurally be legal. FastBackend reuses the normalization already computed by parse when counting AST complexity instead of normalizing twice.

Additional bounded worker-window registration RPC was implemented and tested for changed content, masks and process restarts. It uses content digests (including nested halos), worker cache cap 35% of its existing memory budget, cache-miss re-registration, and direct-RPC fallback for oversized windows. It is OFF by default and explicitly false in all staged configs: a five-real-formula, 32-train-window, 160-fit replay matched coefficients/R2 but took 6.44s vs direct-RPC 6.24s, so no acceleration claim is made. Transfer savings did not exceed hashing/registration costs in that sample.

72 CPU server regressions passed. GPU0 fixed-token batch4 logits comparison at 32/128/256 positions matched within rtol/atol 2e-4; observed maximum absolute difference 8.6e-6. At 256 tokens, full-prefix forward sequence took 1.464s vs KV 0.809s (~1.81x); 128 tokens 0.553 vs 0.390s (~1.42x). First 32-token measurement includes initialization effects and is not a steady-state speedup claim. Same-seed constrained sampling records matched exactly for the benchmark stream; this is not a universal bitwise reproducibility guarantee near multinomial decision boundaries. Peak allocated GPU memory in the test was 563MiB, within 5% GPU0 cap. Timing on a shared device is variable; these are inference-only, not whole-training results.

Files `kv-benchmark.json`, `rpc-benchmark.json`, and `all-optimization-tests.log` hold evidence. No mixed precision, approximate least-squares solver, data subsampling beyond the approved coarse stage, changed SFT schedule, or reduced success budget was introduced. Full-model training/checkpoint I/O, remaining symbolic simplification and dataset integrity checks remain unchanged; no unsupported claim of having eliminated every possible bottleneck is made.
